- White/gray downy or powdery coating on the leaf surface — characteristic of fungal sporangiophore growth
- Yellow-green chlorotic patches on the upper leaf surface
- Leaf tissue appears wilted/damaged but not soft/rotted
- The angular lesion pattern bounded by veins is consistent with Downy Mildew

**Ruling out other classes:**
- **Alternaria Leaf Spot**: Would show circular dark spots with concentric rings and yellow halos — not present
- **Bacterial Soft Rot**: Would show slimy, water-soaked, soft lesions turning dark brown/black — not present
- **Black Rot**: Would show V-shaped yellow lesions at leaf margins with blackened veins — not the dominant pattern

The white/gray downy growth combined with yellow chlorotic patches on the upper leaf surface is the hallmark presentation of **Downy Mildew** (*Peronospora parasitica*) on cauliflower.
